original_question: Consider a generic pair of smooth vector fields f_0 and f_1 near a point q_0 in R^2 such that f_0(q_0) and f_1(q_0) are collinear, n_2(q_0) = 1, and n_3(q_0) = 2, and define the almost-Riemannian distance S_{q_0}(q) as the minimum time needed to reach q from q_0 along trajectories of q˙ = u_0 f_0(q) + u_1 f_1(q) under the unit-norm constraint on the two control components stated in the paper. What is the C^1-classification of the germ of the distance function S_{q_0} for such generic pairs?
target_in_paper: Section IV, "Unfolding the sub-Riemannian distance," specifically the final 2-dimensional almost-Riemannian open problem: classify, for generic pairs of smooth vector-field germs on R^2 with f0(q0) ∧ f1(q0) = 0, n2(q0) = 1, and n3(q0) = 2, the germs of the almost-Riemannian distance S_{q0}. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target: it has the correct ambient space R^2, the germ-at-q0 setup, the collinearity condition f0(q0) ∧ f1(q0) = 0, the bracket-growth hypotheses n2(q0) = 1 and n3(q0) = 2, the control system dot q = u0 f0(q) + u1 f1(q) with u0^2 + u1^2 = 1, and the fact that the goal is a C^1-classification of the resulting distance germ. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem to find or determine the classification, not as a problem with a classification already supplied. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

To make the question stand-alone, you should define n_k(q) as the span at q of all iterated Lie brackets of f0 and f1 of length at most k; this notation is introduced earlier in Section II, not in the final Section IV sentence itself. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

It is slightly more faithful to the paper to speak of smooth (C^∞) germs of vector fields at q0, rather than merely vector fields near q0. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The classification problem ranges over generic pairs among those satisfying the tangency and bracket-growth conditions; it is not asking for one normal form attached to a single unspecified pair. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

If the question is to be fully self-contained, the notion of C^1-classification should be made explicit. The paper spells out C^1-equivalence immediately above for sphere germs via ambient C^1-diffeomorphisms, but does not restate the function-germ version in the final 2-dimensional sentence, so this point is implicit in the nearby context. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

For full control-theoretic completeness, you may state that admissible controls are measurable and admissible trajectories are Lipschitz, as in the surrounding setup of the paper. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
refined_question: Let q0 ∈ R^2, and let f0, f1 be smooth (C^∞) germs of vector fields at q0. For each k ≥ 1, let n_k(q) denote the span at q of all iterated Lie brackets of f0 and f1 of length at most k. Assume that f0(q0) ∧ f1(q0) = 0, n2(q0) = 1, and n3(q0) = 2. Define S_{q0}(q) to be the almost-Riemannian distance from q0 to q, i.e. the minimal time needed to steer q0 to q by a Lipschitz trajectory of dot q = u0 f0(q) + u1 f1(q) with measurable controls satisfying u0^2 + u1^2 = 1. Determine the generic C^1-equivalence classes of the function germ S_{q0} at q0 arising from such pairs (f0, f1). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
justification: This is the exact final open question in Section IV, introduced as a 2-dimensional modification that, in Agrachev's words, already contains the main difficulty of the higher-dimensional unfolding problem. Your draft tracks the paper closely, but it leaves the definition of n_k(q) implicit, does not explicitly preserve the fact that this is an unsolved classification problem over a generic family of pairs, and does not spell out the nearby implicit notion of C^1-equivalence. The paper also explicitly points to reference [10] for partial results on this 2-dimensional almost-Riemannian tangency setting. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
